title: How would you set up an AI day-trading workflow, and any good free real-time data?
author: Exciting-Topic3902
selftext: Does anyone know how to set up a workflow for day traders? I want to use my Grok Bot AI to day trade, but I'm not sure how to set up the system. Should I make an initial system bot on my PC or in the cloud, like a filter and stuff, and then let that connect into the Grok Bot to make the final decision? Or do you guys know any good free data to access the market, so the data can be fed second by second, very quickly?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
keep grok out of the second-by-second loop. a model call takes a few seconds, so by then the move is gone. a plain script on your pc or a cheap vps does the filter and the stops, and the AI only sees the shortlist and says yes or no. alpaca's free plan streams IEX quotes over a websocket for data.

that paper half is why Quantradin exists. I built it as somewhere an agent can trade fake money on real prices before anyone trusts it. quantradin.com

what timeframe are you planning on?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I'd keep the hard rules in plain code on your PC or a small cloud box, like the entry filter, position size and daily loss limit, and use the AI only as a last check that can say no, not as the one deciding. Anything that costs money shouldn't depend on a chatbot's answer. Truly free real-time data every second is rare and usually delayed or limited, and for day trading that delay can break a strategy, so I'd start with slower bars and paper trading to see what the system really does. Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance.

comments.author: Due_Set_6523
comments.body:
Don’t let the LLM handle the fast part. Have code scan the data and flag setups that meet your rules, then send only those to Grok for a second opinion. LLM calls are too slow for second-by-second data.

Put your risk rules (size, stop loss, daily loss limit) in code too, not the prompt.

For data: crypto exchanges mostly have free real-time websockets. Free stock data is usually delayed, so check before you trust it.

Paper trade it first.
